coverage_note: No echo-candidates file for 09-15. Long Latin-transliterated stretches (06:00-11:40, 18:00-21:10, 47:00-1:05:30). Engine mishearings: 26:47 عطلوا = 2aatalu; 30:17 طيار = 8ayyar; 31:39 طيرنا = 8ayyarna; 41:58 بوتنا likely 5u66atna; 39:52 الآن = el-alwaan. Skipped as S4/self-fix: 02:04 ما تفي, 14:57 كسروا->انكسروا, 17:13 اكسرو->ما تكسرو, 31:50 بنغير->نغير, 44:18 شعرها->شعرك, 44:20 شهر (ع->ه pronunciation). 35:34 'Program is feminine' was a meta remark before any Arabic, left out. 54:07 bisawar: Amal said she heard يصور, not a slip. 01:24 بتيت was a question about a word, not a slip.

rows.medi_said: [answering من وين بتشتغل اليوم] أناا بدأت شغلي على تسعة ونص
rows.wrong: على تسعة ونص (answered when, not where)
rows.why: He misunderstood her question من وين as 'when'; she pointed out it is 'where' - a listening miss, not a wrong word.
rows.english: I started work at 9:30 (answering 'from where are you working today')

rows.medi_said: معروف is ground؟ ... What was it؟ What was ground؟
rows.why: He could not find the word for ground meat, guessed معروف/مرفوف and asked; she supplied مفروم.
لحم is masculine; he switched to the feminine مفرومة and she answered with مفروم.
Vegetables (plural, treated feminine) need مختلفة; he hesitated and settled on masculine مختلف, she said only طيب.

rows.amal_said: Yeah, we don't say that yesterday. Just yesterday is its own...
rows.why: He put el- on امبارح; she explained yesterday never takes el- (repeated at 05:52 الأمبارح, one row).
He used the present/I-form aji for 'he came'; she recast to the past أجا and he repeated Aja.
'Came to my house' takes 3ala/3ind, not min; she said 'la, aja 3ala' and he repeated aja ala beiti.

rows.medi_said: Aja andi wu rah bad, um, metakhri.
rows.why: For 'went home late' she recast raa7 to rawwa7 (go home) and said it is the better word, though she also said rah is عادي - may be a both-fine case.
rows.english: he came to my place and went home late

rows.medi_said: Uh, but fatad means, like, you choose? ... So I know bafadal.
rows.amal_said: امتى بتفضل؟ ... You don't know بفضل؟ ... بفضل I prefer.
rows.why: He did not recognise بتفضل in her question and asked what it meant; she explained بفضل = I prefer.
Asked whether he liked yesterday's practice, he answered with a wrong-person form (engine: haketni); she gave حبيت.

rows.medi_said: احنا بنفضل انه انت ... ما بتكسري. ما، ما بتس-- بتكس،
rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih
rows.why: After بنفضل (prefer) the second verb drops its b-; she recast ما تكسري and he repeated it.
rows.english: we prefer that you don't break it

rows.why: 'Why did they break them' needs the they-ending (kasaruhom); he said kasarhom (he broke them), she only said Mm-hmm and typed the fix (chat alone is not a correction).

rows.medi_said: شو كسرهم. No. شو نكس-- uh, انكسرهم. ... Oh, شو انكسرهم.
rows.why: With an object (broke them) the verb is the active كسر, not the n- form انكسر; she re-asked twice and then said شو كسرهم.

rows.amal_said: تكسري. What's plural of أشي إشي؟ ... تكسري أشياء.
rows.why: 'Things' is plural; she asked for the plural of إشي and gave أشياء.
rows.english: since when do you break things?

rows.why: He said سنين (years) for teeth; she gave سنان and asked what سنين means, he answered 'year'.
He blended kaasa (cup) with kasar into an invented plural kasaraat; she recast kasaat and he accepted 'that's right'.

rows.medi_said: الولاد عطلوا ... عطلوا ما بعد واحدة.
rows.amal_said: قتلهو. They fought who? قتلوا بعض. ... They fought each other.
rows.why: He left 'fought' without its object / used ma ba3d; she asked 'they fought who?' and gave قاتلوا بعض (engine wrote عطلوا for 2aatalu).
rows.proposed_rule: 'Each other' is ba3ad straight after the verb, no ma3: 2aatalu ba3ad = they fought each other.

rows.medi_said: واحدة ال-- واحد الولاد. ... واحد من ولاد.
rows.amal_said: واحد of the children ... or of them. One of them.
rows.why: 'Of the children' needs el- (min el-wlaad); she rephrased in English and he then said واحد منهم / واحد من الولاد.
'My mind' needs the possessive -i; she recast رأيي.
'What changed your mind' needs -ak on ra2y; she prompted 'your mind' (engine wrote طيار for غيّر).

rows.amal_said: we just should. we not should have.
rows.why: He started with kaan laazem (should have) for 'we should'; she said it is just should, not should have.
rows.english: we should change the flight time

rows.why: After لازم the verb is a bare present; he used the past 8ayyarna (engine wrote طيرنا), she said 'present, مضارع' and he gave نغير.

rows.amal_said: very close. بس السيارة، السيارة feminine or masculine؟ غيرت.
rows.why: طيارة is feminine so the verb needs the she-ending; she asked the gender and he said تغيرت.
She asked for formal shoes; he used بوت (sheet: 'sneakers / boots | Boat') and she prompted the other word, he gave كندرتك (sheet: 'formal shoes | Kundara'); her chat accepts both.
rows.english: why didn't you change your shoes?

rows.why: For 'our plans' the engine wrote بوتنا (boots); she said Perfect and typed 5u66atna, so most likely the engine misheard him.

rows.amal_said: تغير أو تغيري حالك أو حالك. Make it consistent. Make the gender consistent.
rows.why: He mixed a masculine verb with a feminine حالِك; she named the gender-consistency rule (he says he said تغيري, she heard تغير).
Day-of-the-meeting is idafa so the first word drops el-; he started اليوم, she prompted and he gave يوم الاجتماع.
rows.english: why did the meeting day change?

rows.amal_said: It did change. Why did it change? It did change.
rows.why: He used a present form for 'did change'; she stressed 'it did change' in English and he said past تغير.
rows.english: why did the meeting day change?

rows.amal_said: Again. Photograph me. You photograph me.
rows.why: 'Photograph me' is the doubled command صوّريني, not the get-photographed t- form; she said 'again' and he gave صوريني.

rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. That's the error I was talking about. So cam takes singular.
rows.why: After kam the noun is singular; she named the rule and he said kam sura.
rows.english: how many pictures did you take?

rows.medi_said: wasn't it just bitsawri, bitsawri kateer?
rows.why: 'Get photographed' needs the t- form btetsawwari; she contrasted بتصور/بتتصوري and he said bitsitsawri.
rows.english: do you get photographed a lot?

rows.why: The ordinary present 'knows' needs b- (her chat bye3raf); she said nothing about it.

rows.amal_said: First do the left, left past. Make it past.
rows.why: 'When I travelled the world' is past; he started with a present form and she told him to make it past, he said lavit.
rows.english: when I went around the world

rows.medi_said: How do you feel with this shuba test or...?
rows.amal_said: we would use the شو بتحس ... what do you feel like now? We would say شو حاسس
rows.why: He asked in English; she taught شو حاسس (how are you feeling now) as a new phrase.

rows.medi_said: So you add the E. It's Zakarini.
rows.amal_said: Less e. ... there's two doubled in smack in the middle of the verb
rows.why: For the command 'remind me' he added an extra vowel; she said 'less e' because of the doubled middle.

rows.amal_said: I bring. ... To bring, but who's bringing? You are bringing.
rows.why: 'Remind me to bring' - the bringer is him, so I-form ajib, not the you-f jibi; she asked who is bringing and he said Ajib.
'Him' rides on the verb as -o; he gave -ik (you) then a wrong -no, she repeated the English and then gave zakkarto.

rows.medi_said: so it zakara, uh, it zakarooni.
rows.why: 'They didn't remember me' needs ma; she stressed 'didn't' and he added maate.

rows.medi_said: Huwe ma hazakar. Ma id zakar.
rows.why: Habitual present 'doesn't remember' keeps b-; she recast ma byetzakkar and he said 'it's present tense'.
His plural of 'name' came out as asayam (engine; perhaps أسامي); she gave asmaa.

rows.amal_said: As it's general, so what do we add? ... Il asma.
rows.why: General nouns take el-; she asked what to add, he did not know and she supplied il-asma.

rows.amal_said: الكل؟ ... كل الكلمات؟ كل شي. You could say كل شي.
rows.why: He used el-kul (everyone) for 'everything/all of it'; she questioned الكل؟ and offered كل شي.
